x: The 16th Finance Commission (2026-31) raised the urban share of local-body grants from 36% to 45% (about ₹3.6 lakh crore for ULBs against ₹4.4 lakh crore for rural local bodies). 36% was the earlier share; 35%, 40% and 50% are not the figures.

Part VII (party in power) bars combining official visits with electioneering, using official machinery or transport, and announcing new schemes or grants once polls are announced (options A, B, C). Ordinary official visits not combined with electioneering are not restricted, so D is the answer.

Postal ballot covers service voters, special voters, electors on election duty and those in preventive detention; absentee voters include seniors aged 85+, persons with 40%+ benchmark disability and essential-service staff on duty. Private-sector employees as a class, irrespective of election duty, are not a listed category, so A.

All three are alternative criteria (any one suffices) under the Election Symbols Order, 1968: State-party recognition in 4 or more States; 6% of valid votes in 4 States plus 4 Lok Sabha seats; or 2% of Lok Sabha seats from at least 3 States. In APPSC-G2 2025 all listed conditions were valid, so the key there was 'None of the above' (none invalid). Options A, B and C each leave out a valid criterion.

Balwantrai Mehta made the Collector the chairman of the Zilla Parishad. Later committees split on the Collector's role, and none of them (Ashok Mehta, Hanumantha Rao or G.V.K. Rao) is correctly paired with the statement shown, so only A is correctly matched.

All three are correct: eGramSwaraj was launched along with SVAMITVA on 24 April 2020; SVAMITVA is implemented by the Survey of India; and it gives a 'Record of Rights' for rural homes plus a property-tax baseline. So D.
The Backward Regions Grant Fund (BRGF) was merged into RGSA (APPSC-GS 2018). RGSA converges with Mission Antyodaya rather than absorbing it; SVAMITVA and MPLADS are separate schemes.

Section 125 of the RPA 1951 deals with promoting enmity between classes in connection with elections. Security deposits are under Section 34, party registration under Section 29A, and the exit-poll ban under Section 126A.

The Election Commission of India was set up on 25 January 1950, a day before the Constitution came into force; this date is observed as National Voters' Day since 2011. 26 January 1950 is Republic Day, not the ECI's foundation day.
India's first general election was held in 1951-52 (the 1st Lok Sabha is dated 1952); it and the next three (1957, 1962, 1967) were held simultaneously with Assembly polls.
